nodes.summary:
For modal formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the conjunction $\varphi \wedge \psi$ is the formula $
eg(\varphi 	o 
eg\psi)$, where $
eg\chi$ stands for $\chi 	o  ot$.
nodes.title: Conjunction

nodes.summary:
For a modal formula $\varphi$, the symmetry axiom B is the formula $\varphi 	o \Box\Diamond\varphi$, where $\Diamond\psi$ is $
eg\Box
eg\psi$ and $
eg\chi$ stands for $\chi 	o  ot$.
nodes.title: Axiom B

nodes.summary:
For a modal formula $\varphi$, the seriality axiom D is the formula $\Box\varphi 	o \Diamond\varphi$, where $\Diamond\psi$ is $
eg\Box
eg\psi$ and $
eg\chi$ stands for $\chi 	o  ot$.
nodes.title: Axiom D

nodes.summary:
For a modal formula $\varphi$, the euclidean axiom 5 is the formula $\Diamond\varphi 	o \Box\Diamond\varphi$, where $\Diamond\psi$ is $
eg\Box
eg\psi$ and $
eg\chi$ stands for $\chi 	o  ot$.
nodes.title: Axiom 5

nodes.summary: For a modal formula $\varphi$, the transitivity axiom 4 is the formula $\Box\varphi \to \Box\Box\varphi$.
nodes.title: Axiom 4

nodes.summary: For modal formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the distribution axiom K is the formula $\Box(\varphi \to \psi) \to (\Box\varphi \to \Box\psi)$.
nodes.title: Axiom K

nodes.summary: For a modal formula $\varphi$, the reflexivity axiom T is the formula $\Box\varphi \to \varphi$.
nodes.title: Axiom T

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $N$ be Kripke models over the same atoms, with sets of worlds $W$ and $V$ and accessibility relations $R_M$ and $R_N$. A bounded morphism from $M$ to $N$ is a map $f : W \to V$ such that every atom holds at a world $w$ in $M$ if and only if it holds at $f(w)$ in $N$; whenever $w \mathrel{R_M} w'$, also $f(w) \mathrel{R_N} f(w')$ (forth); and whenever $f(w) \mathrel{R_N} v'$, there is a world $w'$ with…
nodes.title: Bounded morphism

nodes.summary: Let $M_1$, $M_2$, $M_3$ be Kripke models over the same atoms. If $f$ is a bounded morphism from $M_1$ to $M_2$ and $g$ is a bounded morphism from $M_2$ to $M_3$, then the composite map $g \circ f$ on worlds is a bounded morphism from $M_1$ to $M_3$.
nodes.title: Composition of bounded morphisms

nodes.summary:
For a modal formula $\varphi$, the formula $\Diamond\varphi$ ("possibly $\varphi$") is $
eg\Box
eg\varphi$, where $
eg\chi$ stands for $\chi 	o  ot$.
nodes.title: The possibility operator

nodes.summary: Two bounded morphisms $f$ and $g$ between the same Kripke models are equal if $f(w) = g(w)$ for every world $w$.
nodes.title: Extensionality for bounded morphisms

nodes.summary: For a type $\alpha$ of atoms, the formulas of basic modal logic over $\alpha$ are generated as follows: every atom $p \in \alpha$ is a formula; falsity $\bot$ is a formula; if $\varphi$ and $\psi$ are formulas then so is the implication $\varphi \to \psi$; and if $\varphi$ is a formula then so is the necessity formula $\Box\varphi$.
nodes.title: Modal formulas

nodes.summary: For every Kripke model $M$, the identity map on the worlds of $M$ is a bounded morphism from $M$ to itself.
nodes.title: Identity bounded morphism

nodes.summary: A Kripke model consists of a nonempty collection of worlds, an accessibility relation, and an atom valuation.
nodes.title: Kripke model

nodes.summary: The negation of a modal formula $\varphi$ is the formula $\neg\varphi := \varphi \to \bot$.
nodes.title: Negation of modal formulas

nodes.summary: For every Kripke model $M$, the formula $\bot$ is not valid in $M$: since $M$ has at least one world and no world satisfies $\bot$, some world of $M$ fails to satisfy $\bot$.
nodes.title: Falsity is valid in no Kripke model

nodes.summary: The disjunction of modal formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$ is the formula $\varphi \lor \psi := \neg\varphi \to \psi$, where $\neg\varphi$ is $\varphi \to \bot$.
nodes.title: Disjunction of modal formulas

nodes.summary:
Let $M$ be a Kripke model with accessibility relation $R$, and let $\Diamond\varphi$ denote the formula $
eg\Box
eg\varphi$, where $
eg\chi$ is $\chi 	o  ot$. For every world $w$ and modal formula $\varphi$, $w$ satisfies $\Diamond\varphi$ in $M$ if and only if there is a world $v$ with $w \mathrel{R} v$ such that $v$ satisfies $\varphi$ in $M$.
nodes.title: Semantics of possibility

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a bounded morphism from a Kripke model $M$ to a Kripke model $N$ over the same atoms. Then for every modal formula $\varphi$ and every world $w$ of $M$, $w$ satisfies $\varphi$ in $M$ if and only if $f(w)$ satisfies $\varphi$ in $N$.
nodes.title: Invariance of modal satisfaction under bounded morphisms

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model with accessibility relation $R$. Satisfaction of a modal formula at a world $w$ of $M$ is defined by recursion on the formula: $w$ satisfies an atom $p$ if and only if the valuation of $M$ makes $p$ true at $w$; $w$ never satisfies $\bot$; $w$ satisfies $\varphi \to \psi$ if and only if $w$ satisfies $\psi$ whenever it satisfies $\varphi$; and $w$ satisfies $\Box\varphi$ if and only if…
nodes.title: Satisfaction in a Kripke model

nodes.summary: The formula $\top$ is the negation $\neg\bot$ of falsity, that is, the implication $\bot \to \bot$.
nodes.title: The truth constant

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model whose accessibility relation $R$ is symmetric: $R\,u\,v$ implies $R\,v\,u$ for all worlds $u, v$. Then for every formula $\varphi$ the B axiom $\varphi \to \Box\Diamond\varphi$, where $\Diamond\varphi$ abbreviates $\neg\Box\neg\varphi$, is globally valid in $M$.
nodes.title: Axiom B is valid on symmetric Kripke models

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model whose accessibility relation $R$ is serial: every world $w$ has some world $v$ with $R\,w\,v$. Then for every formula $\varphi$ the D axiom $\Box\varphi \to \Diamond\varphi$, where $\Diamond\varphi$ abbreviates $\neg\Box\neg\varphi$, is globally valid in $M$.
nodes.title: Axiom D is valid on serial Kripke models

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model whose accessibility relation $R$ is euclidean: $R\,u\,v$ and $R\,u\,w$ imply $R\,v\,w$ for all worlds $u, v, w$. Then for every formula $\varphi$ the 5 axiom $\Diamond\varphi \to \Box\Diamond\varphi$, where $\Diamond\varphi$ abbreviates $\neg\Box\neg\varphi$, is globally valid in $M$.
nodes.title: Axiom 5 is valid on euclidean Kripke models

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model whose accessibility relation $R$ is transitive: $R\,u\,v$ and $R\,v\,w$ imply $R\,u\,w$ for all worlds $u, v, w$. Then for every formula $\varphi$ the 4 axiom $\Box\varphi \to \Box\Box\varphi$ is globally valid in $M$.
nodes.title: Axiom 4 is valid on transitive Kripke models

nodes.summary: The K axiom is valid on every Kripke model.
nodes.title: Validity of axiom K on Kripke models

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model whose accessibility relation $R$ is reflexive: $R\,w\,w$ for every world $w$. Then for every formula $\varphi$ the T axiom $\Box\varphi \to \varphi$ is globally valid in $M$.
nodes.title: Axiom T is valid on reflexive Kripke models

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $N$ be Kripke models over the same atoms and let $f$ be a bounded morphism from $M$ to $N$ whose map on worlds is surjective. Then for every formula $\varphi$, $\varphi$ is globally valid in $M$ if and only if $\varphi$ is globally valid in $N$.
nodes.title: Surjective bounded morphisms preserve and reflect validity

nodes.summary: A formula $\varphi$ is globally valid in a Kripke model $M$ when $\varphi$ is satisfied at every world of $M$.
nodes.title: Global validity in a Kripke model

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
